post.description:
Self-serve accounts for the participant and company portals.

Admin is not on this path — a shared access code or an existing staff
account is how platform users get in, so this never creates one.

Deliberately the same response whether or not the address is known -
a different one enumerates who has an account.

schema.title: Response Forgot Password Auth Password Forgot Post

post.description:
A shared-secret shortcut into platform admin.

Disabled unless PROJET_ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE is configured — an unconfigured
deploy gets a 404 rather than a code nobody can guess, so this never reads
as "admin login is broken" versus "this path is off".

get.description:
Unauthenticated probe, so the frontend can render signed-out state
without a 401 in the console on every page load.

schema.title: Response Session Probe Auth Session Get

post.description:
FR-014 — admin creates the company and its first user, the owner.
The owner invites everyone else themselves.

The mark that appears on the challenge the company publishes.

Replacing one writes a new key and drops the old object, so a cached page
never shows the previous logo under the same address.

get.description:
Unsigned on purpose.

The listing and the directory are read without a session, so the logo on
them has to be too. Only raster images are ever stored here, and the media
type comes from the extension we chose at upload rather than from anything
the uploader sent.

FR-018 — everyone who consented, across every programme this company has
run. Consent is enforced by the query, not by this route (section 8).

schema.title: Response Candidate Pool Companies  Company Id  Candidates Get
Response List Users Companies  Company Id  Users Get

post.description: FR-016 — the owner invites a colleague directly. No admin in the loop.

delete.description:
Disabled rather than deleted: their scores and testimonials must keep
their attribution.

put.description: FR-015 — this is what scopes a rep to their own challenge.

schema.title: Response List Clusters Roles Clusters Get

get.description:
FR-043 — search runs across names and aliases, so "data analyst" or "BI"
lands on Data Analytics rather than creating a near-duplicate.

schema.title: Response Search Roles Roles Search Get

get.description:
FR-053 — what picking this role commits them to, before they commit.

The deliverable, the sources, the two role-specific criteria and the
low-friction asks. Seeing the artifact spec now is what prevents discovering
after the cohort ran that it was not what they wanted.

post.description:
Company owners/admins create the programme shell for their own company;
platform staff can create for any company. The rubric is composed
immediately from the role template so slots 2 and 3 arrive pre-filled
(FR-055).

patch.description:
FR-072/074/076 — anchors are editable, universal names are not, and
nothing is editable once judging has started.

post.description:
FR-075 — validation blocks publication with an incomplete rubric, and
the start and end dates run again here, because the company is not the
only caller. The brief and applications-close date are the company's
judgement call, not a gate — see _setup_problems.

Session times are fixed at setup and published in the brief, because
participants are assigned to one at acceptance (FR-811b).

schema.title: Response Add Judging Session Programmes  Programme Id  Judging Sessions Post

get.description:
FR-057/069 — one list, provenance visible per resource.

The company sees what it excluded as well as what it kept, because an
invisible exclusion is indistinguishable from a source that was never there.

schema.title: Response Get Data Pack Programmes  Programme Id  Data Pack Get

post.description: Add a link the company wants participants to work from.

schema.title: Response Add Data Pack Resource Programmes  Programme Id  Data Pack Post

post.description:
The company's own file, not a link to it.

A shared Drive link is a permission the company has to keep right for a
week; an upload is a copy we can serve, expire, and stop serving when the
programme ends. Stored under a signed key, so a forwarded URL dies.

schema.title: Response Upload Data Pack Resource Programmes  Programme Id  Data Pack Upload Post

patch.description: Include, exclude, rename, or reclassify one entry.

schema.title: Response Update Data Pack Resource Programmes  Programme Id  Data Pack  Resource Id  Patch

delete.description: Remove a resource the company put on this programme.

post.description:
FR-061 — two or three angles on the role, from research on the company.

The company runs this themselves, and admin can run it for them: both pass
this guard, and the company account is the one thing everything hangs off.

Nothing is auto-published (FR-063). The angles land in a review list, the
company picks one, and whoever is editing rewrites it before it runs.

schema.title: Response Draft Problem Statement Endpoint Programmes  Programme Id  Problem Statement Draft Post

get.description: Every angle drafted so far, newest run first, angles in offered order.

schema.title: Response List Drafts Programmes  Programme Id  Problem Statement Drafts Get

put.description:
FR-063/FR-067 — admin reviews and rewrites, and a company that knows
exactly what it wants can say so and have that be what runs.

get.description: FR-301 — filterable by status, sortable by score.

schema.title: Response List Applications Programmes  Programme Id  Applications Get

patch.description:
FR-302 — auto-saving inline scoring. Admin-only: the prescreen rubric is
never shown to companies or applicants (FR-079).

post.description:
FR-304 — bulk offer, waitlist and reject, each firing its email.

Company self-serve is the default (CLAUDE.md): who runs their own
programme, including who to admit, is the company's call, not something
that has to go through platform staff. `require_company_manager` lets
platform staff act for a company too, the same as everywhere else.
Scoring the prescreen rubric stays platform-only below — FR-079 keeps
that number itself from ever reaching a company or applicant — but the
admission decision it feeds into does not need to.
FR-401 — tokenised, no login. One click from an email.

FR-403 — declining releases the seat and fires waitlist promotion
immediately.

get.description:
FR-1051 - the judging day list, in the order people pitch.

Every non-excluded seat appears here, including people who declined
recruitment sharing. That consent only gates the candidate pool later.

schema.title: Response List Submission Cards Programmes  Programme Id  Submissions Get

patch.description:
Auto-saving, like the prescreen rubric. A judge is watching a pitch, not
filling in a form, so nothing waits on a Save they will forget to press.

get.description: Your own, not your colleague's. Two reps may each write one.

schema.title: Response Get Testimonial Programmes  Programme Id  Participants  Participant Id  Testimonial Get

put.description:
Optional by design (FR-1053).

A testimonial nobody chose to write is worth more than one everybody was
made to, so this is never required to finish scoring and never prompted for
until a pitch has actually been watched.

post.description:
Draft from endorsed skills and the brief. Does not save or publish.

The model only rearranges facts already on the card. A generated paragraph
is still the company's word, so it lands in the textarea rather than on
the profile.

Turn the evening's scores into the thing participants keep.

Safe to repeat: a judge who finishes their card late still reaches the
profile on the next close.

get.description:
FR-104 — one company's own programmes, e.g. for a careers page.

A draft stays unreachable here too (FR-056) — the same rule as the
single-programme page, just applied across the whole company.

schema.title: Response Company Listing Public X  Company Slug  Get

get.description:
FR-105 — every active programme across companies, for a browse page.

Active means the week is not over yet: both accepting applications (`open`)
and still running with applications shut (`closed`). Complete programmes
drop off. The single-company listing above also shows complete ones, since
a company's own careers page is a different audience.

schema.title: Response Platform Directory Public Challenges Get

post.description:
FR-201 to FR-208.

Submission is allowed with either consent declined (FR-202): declining is a
real choice, not a soft block. No password here — applicants sign in later
via the offer / set-password path once they have a reason to. A signed-in
applicant may reuse the CV already on their profile.
FR-103 — when applications are closed the CTA becomes a capture.

schema.title: Response Notify Me Public X  Company Slug   Programme Slug  Notify Me Post

get.description:
Judge tags, credentials and testimonials, compounded across programmes.

Scores are not here and cannot be: FR-1004 keeps them out of every
participant-facing schema, so a rating never reaches the person rated even
by accident. What they see is the evidence, not the arithmetic.

schema.title: Response List Projects Me Projects Get

post.description:
Start a case study for work this platform never ran.

Counted alongside the verified ones and always shown after them — the
scope decision this whole feature turns on.

Start a case study from a programme they finished.

The organisation, the dates and the brief come across already verified.
The four narrative fields come across empty, because the account of the
work is theirs to write and always was.

Attach the work itself, for work that does not live at a URL.

Stored privately and reachable only through an expiring signed link, and
only when this project's own consent setting allows it.

put.description:
Tag unverified skills on a project.

ProjectSkill is a claim, ProfileSkill is an attestation — separate tables,
so tagging a verified project here never impersonates a judge.

get.description:
The whole taxonomy for the self-declared skill drawer.

No role to rank against here — a self-declared project has none — so
every skill is offered on equal footing and reached by typing, same as
the judge's picker with an empty template (FR-903b).

schema.title: Response Project Skill Options Me Skills Options Get

post.description: Replace the CV on the person record. PDF only, under 5MB.

put.description: FR-802 — checked the moment it is pasted, with the answer inline.

A slot filled by upload rather than a Drive link — a memo is one static
document, not something worth keeping live and editable.

post.description: "I've fixed the sharing setting" — check again without re-pasting.

schema.title: Response List Threads Programmes  Programme Id  Threads Get

get.description: FR-611b — surfaced inline as a participant types, before they post.

schema.title: Response Find Similar Programmes  Programme Id  Threads Similar Get

post.description:
Share something with the whole cohort, with no subject to invent.

Multipart rather than JSON because a file can ride along with the message,
or be the message: "here is the dataset" needs no words.
FR-608/609 — served from platform storage, scoped to the programme.
FR-607 — the rep decides what is general and what is personal.

delete.description: FR-613 — admin can remove any post; removals leave a tombstone.

get.description: FR-612 — unanswered threads, reachable in one click from an email.

schema.title: Response Rep Digest Programmes  Programme Id  Digest Get

get.description:
Section 8 — CVs and snapshots are not publicly addressable.

The signature is scoped to the exact key and expires, so a leaked URL
stops working and cannot be edited to reach a different file.
Database reachable, taxonomy seeded, outbox not backing up (FR-1304).
Non-secret configuration, so a deploy can be checked at a glance.

ActorType.title: ActorType
ActorType.description:
Who is acting. Three identities, each with its own email+password.

Platform staff are deliberately a separate table from company users: a bug
in company scoping should never be able to escalate into cross-tenant access.

ApplicationDetail.title: ApplicationDetail
ApplicationDetail.description: FR-303 — writeup and CV side by side, without leaving the list.

ClusterOut.title: ClusterOut
ClusterOut.description:
FR-052 — cluster first, then role.

A flat list of 75 is unusable; picking "Finance" then "Venture Capital" is
two taps and prevents mis-tagging.

CompanyHome.title: CompanyHome
CompanyHome.description: FR-017 — what a company user sees on signing in.

CredentialOut.title: CredentialOut
CredentialOut.description:
Who stood behind which skills, on which programme.

Completion stamps and verify codes stay off this schema: a credential the
holder cannot explain is a log entry, and the evidence is the endorsement.

Dashboard.title: Dashboard
Dashboard.description: FR-501 to FR-507 — what do I do, by when, and where.

confidential.title: Confidential
confidential.description: Behind an acknowledgement, and never named in the public listing.

DataPackResourceUpdate.title: DataPackResourceUpdate
DataPackResourceUpdate.description: Every field optional: this is the include/exclude toggle as much as an edit.

admin_notes.title: Admin Notes
admin_notes.description: Anything from the intake conversation worth grounding the draft in

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.description: Twelve pitches is a comfortable evening; thirty is four hours.

Portfolio.title: Portfolio
Portfolio.description:
What the participant keeps (FR-1201).

Deliberately separate from ProfileOut, which is the editable account. Nothing
on this page is editable, because nothing on it is the participant's claim:
every line was put there by a practitioner who watched them work.

ProgrammeChoice.title: ProgrammeChoice
ProgrammeChoice.description:
One programme the signed-in person is on — for switching when several
are active at once.

start_at.title: Start At
start_at.description: First day. Stored as 00:00 in the programme timezone.

submit_deadline_at.title: Submit Deadline At
submit_deadline_at.description: Last day. Stored as 23:59 in the programme timezone.

ProgrammeUpdate.title: ProgrammeUpdate
ProgrammeUpdate.description: The company picks the days; times of day are pinned on the server.

ProjectEntryOut.title: ProjectEntryOut
ProjectEntryOut.description:
One project card.

`verified` is the only thing on here the participant cannot set, and it is
the thing the whole card is read against, so it is a field of its own.

ProjectEntryUpdate.title: ProjectEntryUpdate
ProjectEntryUpdate.description:
Every field optional; only the ones sent are changed.

A verified entry accepts the description and consent fields and rejects
the rest with a named error (see `update_entry`) — never a silent no-op on
a field the request thought it was changing.

ProjectLinkOut.title: ProjectLinkOut
ProjectLinkOut.description:
A URL or an uploaded file. `file_url` is a signed, expiring link and is
only ever populated for a file.

PublicListing.title: PublicListing
PublicListing.description:
FR-101 — company, role, summary, dates, commitment, and what they get.

The full rubric renders here (FR-078): publishing it tells participants what
they are judged on and removes the "it felt arbitrary" complaint. There is
no advantage in concealing it — the rubric rewards things that cannot be faked.

PublicListingSummary.title: PublicListingSummary
PublicListingSummary.description:
FR-104/FR-105 — the row shape for both listing endpoints below.

Deliberately thinner than `PublicListing`: a browsing stranger picking
between programmes does not need the rubric or the data pack yet, only
enough to decide whether to open the full page.

PublicProjectLink.title: PublicProjectLink
PublicProjectLink.description: A URL, or a signed expiring link to an uploaded file.

RoleImplications.title: RoleImplications
RoleImplications.description:
FR-053 — what the company sees the moment they pick a role.

This is where the programme stops being abstract for the buyer, and it
prevents the common failure where a company picks a role whose deliverable
is not what they actually wanted.

ScoringCard.title: ScoringCard
ScoringCard.description: The rubric for this pitch, with the submission kept alongside it.

ScoringUpdate.title: ScoringUpdate
ScoringUpdate.description: Partial by design: a judge fills this in a value at a time, live.

SetPasswordConfirm.title: SetPasswordConfirm
SetPasswordConfirm.description:
Same shape as a reset, different purpose: a freshly invited account
choosing its first password rather than replacing one.

SubmissionCard.title: SubmissionCard
SubmissionCard.description: One participant, what they handed in, and where their scoring stands.
